extracted.intended_audience: students, researchers, and readers in philosophy of mathematics and constructive mathematics (esp. those studying Brouwer/intuitionism)
extracted.subtask_description: An encyclopedic entry summarizing Brouwerian intuitionism: its foundational principles (the two acts, Creating Subject), semantic/constructive accounts of proof (BHK), formal/intuitive axioms (IQC, continuity axioms, bar/fan theorems), and mathematical consequences (continuum, continuity, counterexamples).

rubrics_metrics.name: The two acts of intuitionism
rubrics_metrics.description: Brouwer's basic foundational moves: (1) completely separating mathematics from mathematical language and taking the basic intuition of mathematics to be the empty form arising from the perception of a move of time (the first act) and (2) admitting two ways of creating new mathematical entities, notably infinite sequences generated by free choice (choice sequences) and mathematical species (the second act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how the first act yields the natural numbers and restricts reasoning (rejecting excluded middle), while the second act establishes the continuum via choice sequences; distinguishes Brouwer's view from Platonism and formalism and from other constructivisms that limit infinite constructions to computable rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Creating Subject
rubrics_metrics.description: An idealized mind in which mathematics takes place, abstracting away inessential human limitations; used to formulate arguments (including Kripke's Schema) and counterexamples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to justify certain arguments and show some classical principles false; formalizations of the Creating Subject make the temporal aspect of intuitionistic truth conspicuous. Its role is important for some arguments but less central historically than the two acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematics as mental construction; time as a priori
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematics is a languageless creation of the mind; time is the only a priori notion (Kantian sense) and mathematical truth consists in mental constructions (proofs/constructions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leads to a conception of truth tied to constructive mental acts and to temporality: a statement may later become provable and hence gain truth; this underlies rejection of certain classical principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection of the principle of the excluded middle (A ∨ ¬A)
rubrics_metrics.description: In intuitionism the principle (A ∨ ¬A) is not generally valid: A statement is true only if there is a proof, and ¬A means a construction deriving falsum from any putative proof of A, so many statements (e.g. open mathematical problems) are neither provable nor refutable at a given time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The BHK-interpretation and examples (Goldbach, Riemann) illustrate how excluded middle fails until a proof or refutation is constructed; continuity axioms can even make quantified forms of excluded middle false.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brouwer–Heyting–Kolmogorov (BHK) interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: An informal account of what counts as an intuitionistic proof: ⊥ not provable; proof of A ∧ B consists of proofs of A and B; proof of A ∨ B is a proof of A or of B; proof of A → B is a construction transforming any proof of A into a proof of B; proof of ∃x A(x) presents a witness d and a proof of A(d); proof of ∀x A(x) is a construction that transforms any proof that d is in the domain into a proof of A(d); ¬A ≡ A → ⊥.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not formal (construction is not precisely defined) but captures intuitionistic practice and forces rejection of excluded middle in many cases; serves as a semantic/intuitive standard for what counts as a proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intuitionistic quantifier logic (IQC) / axiomatization
rubrics_metrics.description: Intuitionistic logic often presented as 'classical logic without excluded middle' (denoted IQC) with a Hilbert-style axiomatization (list of implication/quantifier axioms given in the entry) and Modus Ponens as the rule of inference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IQC is widely used as the logic of constructivism; various proof systems (Gentzen, natural deduction) and semantics (Kripke, Beth, Heyting algebras, topological, categorical) serve to study it. The possibility that new intuitionistic principles might be discovered is acknowledged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disjunction Property (DP)
rubrics_metrics.description: DP: IQC ⊢ A ∨ B implies IQC ⊢ A or IQC ⊢ B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A hallmark differentiating intuitionistic from classical logic; classical logic can prove A ∨ ¬A for independent formulas, violating DP. DP clarifies constructive content of disjunctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status of Ex Falso Sequitur Quodlibet (⊥ → A)
rubrics_metrics.description: The inclusion of Ex Falso (from contradiction anything follows) in intuitionistic logic is discussed; some argue it is not valid in Brouwer's original views and that relevance logic might better capture Brouwer's valid principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SEP entry notes debate and references (van Atten 2008, van Dalen 2004) — this is a point of interpretive nuance rather than settled technical rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural numbers: potential infinity and induction
rubrics_metrics.description: The natural numbers arise from the first act (perception of temporal moves); intuitionism treats all infinity as potential rather than completed, but the principle of induction is fully acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many finite arithmetical truths coincide with classical results (e.g., every natural number has a prime factorization), but quantification over naturals requires care; some complex combinatorial theorems have nontrivial intuitionistic proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weak counterexamples
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructions (introduced by Brouwer) showing that certain classical statements are currently unacceptable intuitionistically; e.g., real numbers r defined so r=0 ⇔ ∀n A(n), producing cases where (r=0 ∨ r≠0) fails intuitionistically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to demonstrate loss of classical theorems (law of trichotomy, intermediate value theorem) in a direct way; distinguish between 'not currently provable' and 'intuitionistically refutable' (¬(A ∨ ¬A) is typically false whereas ¬¬(A ∨ ¬A) is true).

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice sequences (lawlike vs lawless)
rubrics_metrics.description: Infinite sequences created step-by-step: lawlike sequences are determined by a rule/algorithm; lawless sequences are generated freely (e.g., by choice or coin tosses) and are never finished; every real number is represented by a choice sequence in Brouwer's framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choice sequences underlie the intuitionistic continuum and motivate continuity axioms; lawless sequences provide the intuition for potential infinity and explain why some classical distinctions fail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weak continuity axiom (WC-N)
rubrics_metrics.description: WC-N: ∀α ∃n A(α,n) → ∀α ∃m ∃n ∀β ∈ α(¯m) A(β,n). (If for every sequence α there exists n with A(α,n), then n can be chosen based only on a finite initial segment of α.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justified more persuasively for lawless sequences: any choice of n must be made after a finite initial segment is known; WC-N is consistent and often applied where A refers only to α's values (not higher-order properties).

rubrics_metrics.name: Full continuity axiom (C-N)
rubrics_metrics.description: C-N: ∀α ∃n A(α,n) → ∃Φ ∈ CF ∀α A(α,Φ(α)), where CF is the class of continuous functionals assigning naturals to sequences (i.e., Φ depends only on a finite initial segment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stronger than WC-N; implies striking consequences such as the quantified excluded middle being false and the theorem 'every total real function is continuous.' It is central to the intuitionistic conception of the continuum but controversial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neighborhood functions (representation of continuous functionals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuous functionals on sequences can be represented by neighborhood functions f on finite sequences satisfying: α ∃n f(α(¯n)) > 0 and ∀n∀m (f(n) > 0 → f(n·m) = f(n)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interprets when a finite initial segment suffices to compute Φ(α): f(α(¯n)) = 0 means more input needed; f(...)=m+1 means value m determined. Recasts C-N in terms of existence of f ∈ K with specified properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bar theorem, Fan theorem (FAN), and Bar Induction (BI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bar theorem (bar principle) and its corollary Fan theorem (FAN): FAN: ∀α ∈ T ∃n A(α(¯n)) → ∃m ∀α ∈ T ∃n ≤ m A(α(¯n)). BI (Bar Induction) is a well-foundedness/induction principle for spreads (trees) with decidability conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fan theorem yields classical-analogue results like uniform continuity of continuous functions on a closed interval; Brouwer's bar theorem uses assumptions about canonical/well-ordered forms of proofs and is philosophically and technically controversial. BI and FAN are essential to recover parts of analysis within intuitionism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequence: Every total real function is continuous (C-N theorem)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under C-N (continuity axiom) one can prove that every total real function is continuous; classically pathological functions (e.g., Dirichlet function distinguishing rationals/irrationals) are not legitimate intuitionistically because properties like 'being rational' are not decidable on reals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This theorem captures a central, distinctive mathematical consequence of Brouwerian intuitionism: the intuitionistic continuum has properties not shared by the classical continuum (e.g., nondécomposability).

rubrics_metrics.name: Kripke's Schema (KS) and temporal/constructive schemas
rubrics_metrics.description: KS (as presented): ∃α (A ↔ ∃n α(n)=1), where A ranges over formulas and α over choice sequences; KS can be argued for using the Creating Subject and reflects the temporal/choice-based character of intuitionistic truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: KS and related schemas appear in formalizations of the Creating Subject and interact with choice sequences and continuity principles; their acceptance varies and they have concrete model-theoretic/metamathematical consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal nature of truth and provability
rubrics_metrics.description: In intuitionism truth (and falsity) have a temporal aspect: a statement proven at time t lacks a truth-value before t; established facts remain so. Provability is tied to constructive mental activity over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This temporality explains why some classical tautologies are not globally valid intuitionistically; formalizations of this aspect appear in analyses of the Creating Subject and choice sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intuitionistic continuum and nonclassical properties (law of trichotomy fails)
rubrics_metrics.description: The intuitionistic continuum, modeled via choice sequences and continuity axioms, is both an extension and a restriction of the classical continuum: it exhibits properties classically false (e.g., every total function continuous) and fails classical laws like the law of trichotomy ∀x (x < y ∨ x = y ∨ y < x).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weak counterexamples and continuity/bar principles show how classical theorems of analysis are modified: some are lost, others recovered in constructive approximative forms (e.g., intermediate value theorem replaced by ∀n ∃x |f(x)-c| < 2^{-n}).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and plurality of semantics and models
rubrics_metrics.description: Intuitionistic logic and intuitionistic mathematics are studied with many proof systems and semantics (Kripke models, Beth models, Heyting algebras, topological semantics, categorical models, realizability, sheaf models, etc.), and different constructive theories accept different subsets of Brouwerian principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This plurality means that acceptance of specific intuitionistic axioms (WC-N, C-N, FAN, BI, KS, status of Ex Falso) can vary by approach; the SEP entry surveys these variations and their metamathematical implications.
